ID: vr-08

Status: DONE

Dependencies: vr-07

Purpose:
Implement the owner's November 18 evening feedback without cloud speech,
system changes, a second application or disruption of a running user instance.

[x] Measure the unchanged Hazel pipeline and inspect safe native female assets.
[x] Improve measured generation/request latency without fabricating animation.
[x] Default to Hazel and expose bounded, actually working voice-shaping controls.
[x] Use a matching feminine native identity and add lightweight procedural hair.
[x] Verify waveform controls, native correspondence, real-browser behavior and performance.
[x] Update book, tracking, causal ledger and owned continuity; publish verified work.

Acceptance criteria:
Hazel is the explicit default; controls change generated speech rather than only
labels, reset predictably, reject invalid settings and keep motion/audio aligned.
No arbitrary SSML, command, file or remote-audio input. Feminine head and hair
are visible in the actual renderer; identity/topology/model contracts match.
Measure speed on a fixed permitted input, preserve audio-clocked controls,
bounded CPU use and prior safety/error behavior. Distinguish functional waveform/
visual checks from human listening and unmeasured anatomical-contact acceptance.

Completion evidence:
Initial unchanged Hazel greeting: 2.75 seconds/83 frames; startup3.586s,
synthesis0.674s, motion1.903s, median network20.97ms/frame on this shared machine.
Dynamic Mark batching executes but first measurements do not show a speed win.
Official Claire2.3.1 model/native topology installed and hash-verified as data.
Claire uses its own140-coefficient skin,169 outputs, strength1.0 and neutral
cp1_neutral/frame212, not Mark coefficients on a warped female silhouette.
Derived-topology warm startup measured0.878s vs original3.586s. RAM caches skip
repeat inference and expression-only synthesis. Claire's bigger network is
slower per new line than Mark; the latency gains are not a faster-model claim.
Actual Hazel pitch/rate/emphasis/EQ waveform changes verified; pitch requests
are engine-dependent. Thirty-one unit/HTTP checks pass; sixteen isolated real
Edge scenarios pass in claire-browser-04, including all three installed voices,
clear-front hair, preview, reset and caches. Final client-ready greeting6.807s
vs exact latest repeat0.059s; server repeat0.00028s. Shared-machine warm startup
samples1.360/1.530/1.449s; these are observations, not latency guarantees.
Inspected actual frontal/turned screenshots. First browser run's final network
assertion misclassified embedded native-audio data icons as external requests;
corrected the classification, retaining the failed receipt. No new dependency
or system-setting change; owned test browser/server/profile cleaned up.

```text
ID: vr-10
Title: Make the female face readable and polished with fluid playback

Status: DONE
Milestone: Clear eyes, nose and lips in a refined connected-mesh presentation, qualified against a 60-fps render target.
Dependencies: vr-08

Purpose:
Address the owner's report that the eyes, nose and mouth are hard to recognize.
Use supplied images only as visual direction, not copied/published artwork.
Performance and fluidity at 60 fps take priority; polygon reduction is authorized.

Tasks:
[x] Preserve recognizable native facial contours in a lighter presentation topology.
[x] Add directional shading, readable eye/lip details and a polished original style.
[x] Preserve original audio-clocked learned speech motion, controls and error handling.
[x] Measure render frame times and qualify visual/functional behavior in isolated Edge.
[x] Update chapter, TODOs, tracking, causal ledger and reviewed release media.

Acceptance criteria:
Actual frontal and turned browser captures clearly distinguish the eyes, nose
and mouth; no reference likeness/artwork is copied or bundled. Render on
requestAnimationFrame with audio-clocked interpolation, keeping model sampling
and generation latency distinct from the 60-fps display target. Measure a
bounded real-browser run rather than promising universal hardware performance.
Reduce topology if necessary without merging touching lips or relabelling a
different model identity. No external runtime, device activation, system change,
personal recording or interruption of an existing user instance.

Completion evidence:
Native inverse subdivision retains 15,375 original skin indices, 30,759 edges
and 30,746 triangles: about 75% fewer vertices than full skin. It preserves
more facial detail than the old voxel surface, not a smaller payload than it.
Directional smooth shading, original static eyes/iris/pupil and cosmetic brows/
lips/cavity implemented; points default off. No reference artwork or new package.
33 unit/HTTP checks and 18 real Edge scenarios pass. Final face-browser-final
records 361 intervals per density: mean16.691ms, p9516.8ms, max16.9ms,
zero over25ms at1x and2x;381actualdraws/density during6.3s looping playback.
Actual frontal/turned/hair-off/speaking PNGs inspected; no page exceptions or
nonlocal page requests. Muted, not human listening or subjective beauty acceptance.
The 83-frame payload is7,656,750bytes; no fabricated lower-payload claim.

Completion log:
2026-11-19 - Owner supplies visual references, requests recognizable polished
female features, authorizes autonomous implementation and prioritizes 60-fps
fluidity over polygon count. Release captures will be refreshed afterward.
2026-11-19 - Native loops and shading qualified at normal/2x density. Eye bounds/
winding and inverse native topology tested; current chapter08 documents source,
tradeoffs, actual display observations and remaining accuracy boundaries.
2026-11-19 - Implementation, qualification, chapter/index/ledger and final
actual release captures complete. Closing finite presentation work; source
publication and first release proceed under vr-09, not subjective acceptance.
```
